---
title: "Documentation"
---

## Why Documentation Matters

By now, you've called quite a few R functions: `mean()`, `round()`, `sum()`, `install.packages()`, `library()`, and
more. Every one of those functions accepts specific arguments, in a specific order, and some of those arguments have
default values you've been relying on without necessarily realizing it.

**Do:** run the code below.

```{webr-r}
round(3.14159, 2)
round(3.14159)
```

**See:** the second line still works, even though we only gave `round()` one input.

**Explain:** `round()`'s second argument, `digits`, has a *default value* built in, so R uses that default whenever
you don't specify your own. But how would you know that, or know what that default value actually is, without
someone telling you?

That's exactly what **documentation** (also called a "help file") is for. Every function that ships with R, and every
function provided by a package distributed through CRAN, comes with documentation describing exactly what it does,
what arguments it accepts, and what those arguments default to. You will refer to documentation constantly. Even
experienced R users look up help files for functions they've used hundreds of times, just to double check an argument
name or default value.

Over this tutorial, you'll learn how to open a function's documentation, how to read the sections it contains, and
how to use that information to correctly call a function you've never seen before.
